blocking_findings.summary: *[CRITICAL] `check_game_over` winner logic inverted when player 2 tops out (server.py:428)**
The `winner` variable assignment `winner = "you" if pid == 1 else "opponent"` is incorrect. When player 2 tops out (`pid=2`), `winner` is set to `"opponent"`. Then:
Player 2 receives `{"winner": "you"}` — **told they WON when they LOST**
Player 1 receives `{"winner": "opponent"}` — **told they lost when they WON**
Trace: `pid=2` → `winner="opponent"` → line 434: `"opponent" if "opponent"=="you" else "you"` → `"you"` (WRONG) → line 440: sends `"opponent"` (WRONG).
Fix: Remove the broken `winner` variable. Send `"opponent"` to the topping-out player and `"you"` to the opponent unconditionally:

`last_tick_time` is shared between both players, but each player has a different `drop_interval` based on their level. When player 2 has a shorter interval (higher level), their ticks reset `last_tick_time`, preventing player 1 from ever accumulating enough elapsed time to receive a gravity tick. Player 1's piece will **never fall** until they hard-drop.

Trace: Player 2 at level 10 (0.325s interval) ticks every ~0.35s, resetting `last_tick_time`. Player 1 at level 1 (1.0s interval) needs 1.0s since last tick, but the timer is always reset before that. Result: Player 1 gets zero gravity.
Fix: Use per-player tick timestamps. Add `last_tick_time: float = time.time()` to `PlayerConnection.__init__`, and check/update per-player in the game loop.
*[MEDIUM] Hold swap failure corrupts board state (game.py:302-309)**

When a hold swap fails (`valid_position` returns False on line 308), the state has already been modified: `can_hold=False`, pieces swapped, position reset to spawn. The function returns `False` but the board is left with an unplaceable piece. The next `tick()` will call `lock_piece()` (line 323) which writes to the grid **without validating positions** (line 206-207), overwriting existing blocks and corrupting the grid.

pass_conditions: **server.py:423-443**: Replace the broken `winner` logic in `check_game_over`. Remove lines 428/434/440 and send `"opponent"` to the topping-out player and `"you"` to the opponent unconditionally.

**server.py:43-49 + 273-310**: Add `self.last_tick_time: float = time.time()` to `PlayerConnection.__init__`, and change the game loop to check/update per-player tick timestamps instead of sharing `last_tick_time`.
**game.py:297-309**: On hold swap failure, restore original state (undo the swap and re-enable `can_hold`) before returning `False`, or handle the failure in the caller.
